newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium spins wheel on Brussels casino.
newsitem.headline: Belgium spins wheel on Brussels casino.

text.p: The Belgian government proposed on Friday new legislation regulating the gaming industry, opening the way for Brussels to host the country's ninth casino.

Candidates to run the casino, including Britain's London Clubs and a consortium of seven of Belgium's other gaming halls, have been lining up for months. The decision will open the way for more formal bidding to start.

The Brussels region hopes to plug a budgetary gap by awarding the new casino a licence and collecting taxes on its turnover. This will in turn help Belgium reduce its overall deficit as required for the planned single European currency.
Under the proposal, casinos will officially remain banned, as under the 1902 law that presently regulates the sector.
However, by listing nine towns (the eight which already house casinos plus Brussels) where they will be permitted the government hopes to clarify what has become in practice a legal grey area.

The proposed new legislation also seeks to regulate other types of gambling, such as the use of slot machines, and the manufacture of gaming equipment. New clauses designed to stop gaming halls being used by money launderers are also included.
